title: Outlook: Copilot insights on selected email text in classic Outlook for Windows
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout details, default and administrator actions match Microsoft's notice, and the documented control paths and licence-assignment API are accurate. It appropriately distinguishes broader Copilot controls from the undocumented Explain This switch and leaves the feature's licence tier open.

claims.claim: The app-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select **Settings**, and then select **Integrated Apps**.
3. Select the **Available Apps** list.
4. Select an app from the **Available Apps** list to open the overview pane.
5. Select **Block app**.

claims.claim: The documented Integrated Apps controls are only available to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.claim: Blocking an app is tenant-wide and prevents all users from using that app in Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application.
claims.quote: When you choose to block an app, it is blocked for all users in your organization. Blocking an app overrides any previous admin deployment or user installation in Microsoft 365 and Outlook so that no one in your organization can use the app.

claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app through Integrated Apps also blocks access for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps management page says blocking affects Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application while Teams honours Teams admin center settings.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook. Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat says Integrated Apps blocking blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook and Copilot Chat on the web.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.claim: The cited app-management pages do not name Explain This or establish whether the block removes its button.
claims.quote: Searched: "User-initiated" "Outlook" Copilot policy disable; "classic Outlook" "Explain This" "insights". Read Manage Copilot Chat and Apps for Microsoft 365 that work across application hosts; neither names Explain This.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for blocking the Copilot app through this Integrated Apps control.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Integrated Apps block app API PowerShell automation; "Integrated Apps" "Block" "Copilot" "PowerShell" API. Read app-management pages and copilotPackage: block excerpt; the latter blocks packages, not the Copilot host app.

claims.claim: The licence-assignment path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the **Billing** > [Licenses] page.
2. Select a product.
3. On the product details page, select **Assign licenses**.

claims.claim: Licence management in the documented admin center route requires at least a License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense assigns or removes licences for a user.
claims.quote:
Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to.
POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request body uses addLicenses to specify licences to add.
claims.quote: addLicenses | [assignedLicense] collection | A collection of [assignedLicense] objects that specify the licenses to add.

claims.claim: The assignLicense request body uses removeLicenses to specify licences to remove.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: The minimum classic Outlook build for this feature is not stated; the notice asks only for the latest version.
